findings.body: This failure is modeled as a plain `Error` subclass with a hand-rolled `_tag` and an unstructured message as its only payload, and it is raised by `throw` rather than through the Effect error channel. Every other failure in `orchestration-v2/` uses `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` with structured attributes, and the cost shows up at the consumer: `http.ts` has to wrap `selectHistoryPageFromCursor` in `selectHistoryPageFromCursorOrError` (try/catch plus an ad-hoc `{ _tag: "ok" | "invalid_cursor" | "error" }` union) instead of failing typed and recovering with `Effect.catchTags`. Consider declaring it with `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` carrying stable structural context (e.g. `cursorLength`, and `threadId` at the wrapping site — not the raw cursor value) with `message` derived from those attributes, having `decodeThreadHistoryCursor`/`selectHistoryPageFromCursor` return `Effect` failures, and dropping the try/catch adapter in `http.ts` in favor of `Effect.catchTags({ InvalidThreadHistoryCursorError: () => failEnvironmentInvalidRequest("invalid_history_cursor") })`. Posted via Macroscope — Effect Service Conventions

🟢 **Low** `orchestration-v2/ContextHandoffService.ts:91` `compactText` can emit an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate when a provider or fork summary truncates text containing an astral character, so the next provider receives a replacement character instead of the original message content. The `slice(0, maxLength - 3)` boundary is measured in code units; truncate by Unicode code points instead, as the legacy path already does. ```suggestion return `${Array.from(compacted).slice(0, maxLength - 3).join("")}...`; ```
